I see you are presenting with shortness of breath, increased abdominal girth, and a large ovarian mass. To understand the extent of your condition, please describe how long these symptoms have been present and if you have experienced any urinary frequency or difficulty breathing when lying flat.

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, Tumor Markers (CA-125, HE4).
REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic Ultrasound, Chest X-Ray, Abdominal CT.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count: WBC 8,500 /μL, Hemoglobin 12.8 g/dL, Platelets 275,000 /μL; Tumor Markers: CA-125 Level Normal; Images: Pelvic Ultrasound shows a large mass in the right ovary; Chest X-Ray shows a right-sided pleural effusion; Abdominal CT not included in provided data.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Ovarian Cancer with Malignant Pleural Effusion. The combination of a large ovarian mass, right-sided pleural effusion (likely causing the shortness of breath), and ascites (increased abdominal girth) is highly suggestive of advanced ovarian malignancy, even with a currently normal CA-125 level.
